names: Successful son of the Shi house

sourceDate.text: 太和三年六月二十六日夜
太和三年六月二十六日夜
朝廷以布為魏博節度使
天祐二年七月十三日夜

units.zh: 列傳第一百三十一史憲誠史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今爲靈武建康人。
units.en: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. His ancestors originally sprang from the Xi people; in his day Shi Xiancheng was reckoned a man of Jiankang in Lingwu.
units.literal: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. Shi Xiancheng — his ancestors came from the Xi barbarians; he is now registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.

units.zh: 祖道德，開府儀同三司、試太常卿、上柱國、懷澤郡王。
units.en: His grandfather Daode had served as Grand General of the Palace with the Honorary Three Excellencies, Acting Minister of Ceremonies, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Huaize.
units.literal: His grandfather Daode held the titles of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, Acting Taichang Qing, Shangzhuguo, and Prince of Huaize commandery.

units.zh: 父周洛，爲魏博軍校，事田季安，至兵馬大使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞、柱國、北海郡王。
units.en: His father Zhouluo was a Weibo army officer under Tian Ji'an and eventually rose to command the army's horse and foot, with the ranks of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Beihai.
units.literal: His father Zhouluo was an officer in the Weibo army, served Tian Ji'an, and rose to Grand Marshal of Cavalry and Infantry, Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and Prince of Beihai commandery.

units.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。
units.en: Xiancheng first made his name through ability and valor, serving beside his father in senior army posts while also holding the post of Investigating Censor.
units.literal: Xiancheng began by virtue of talent and courage; following his father he held senior posts in the army and concurrently served as Investigating Censor.

units.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。
units.en: During the Yuanhe reign, when Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng ahead with four thousand vanguard troops to cross the Yellow River and take one fortified camp after another.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to cross the river with four thousand vanguard troops, repeatedly capturing his fortified camps.

units.zh: 復以大軍齊進，乘勢逐北，魏之全師迫於鄆之城下。
units.en: The main army then advanced in concert, riding the momentum of victory in a northward pursuit until Wei's full force was pinned beneath the walls of Yan.
units.literal: Then with the main force advancing together, they seized the momentum to pursue northward, pressing Wei's entire army to the walls of Yan prefecture.

units.zh: 師道窮蹙，劉悟斬首投魏軍。
units.en: With Shidao driven to desperation, Liu Wu cut off his head and presented it to the Wei forces.
units.literal: Shidao was cornered; Liu Wu beheaded him and surrendered the head to the Wei army.

units.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。
units.en: When his merits were entered on the rolls, Xiancheng was promoted out of turn to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: His achievements were recorded, and Xiancheng was exceptionally promoted to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 鎮州王承宗死，弘正自魏移領鎮州。
units.en: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died, Hongzheng left Wei to assume command of Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhen prefecture died; Hongzheng moved from Wei to take charge of Zhen.

units.zh: 居數月，爲王廷湊所殺，遂以兵叛。
units.en: Within a few months Hongzheng was murdered by Wang Tingcou, who then rose in armed rebellion.
units.literal: After several months he was killed by Wang Tingcou, who then rebelled with troops.

units.zh: 朝廷以弘正子布爲魏博節度使，領兵討伐，俾復父冤。
units.en: The court made Hongzheng's son Bu military governor of Weibo and sent him to campaign against the rebels, that he might avenge his father's death.
units.literal: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Bu as military governor of Weibo and led troops to punish the rebels, so that he might avenge his father.

units.zh: 時幽州硃克融援助廷湊，布不能制，因自引決，軍情囂然。
units.en: Zhu Kerong of Youzhou was then aiding Tingcou; Bu could not master the army, took his own life, and the troops fell into uproar.
units.literal: At the time Zhu Kerong of Youzhou aided Tingcou; Bu could not control the situation and killed himself, and army morale became turbulent.

units.zh: 憲誠爲中軍都知兵馬使，乘亂以河朔舊事動其人心，諸軍即擁而歸魏，共立爲帥，國家因而命之。
units.en: Xiancheng, as chief controller of the central army's horse and foot, used the disorder to appeal to the old ways of the Hebei garrisons; the troops at once rallied back to Wei, set him up as their leader, and the throne confirmed the appointment.
units.literal: Xiancheng was Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry of the central army; exploiting the chaos he stirred the troops' hearts with old customs of the Hebei region, the armies immediately rallied and returned to Wei, jointly installing him as commander, and the state accordingly appointed him.

units.zh: 時克融、廷湊並據兵爲亂，憲誠喜得旄節，雖外順朝旨，而中與硃、王爲輔車之勢，長慶二年正月也。
units.en: Kerong and Tingcou were both in arms against the court; Xiancheng was delighted to receive the commander's baton and banner. Outwardly he followed the court's orders, yet inwardly he and Zhu and Wang lent each other the support of linked chariots — all this in the first month of the second year of Changqing.
units.literal: At the time Kerong and Tingcou both held troops in rebellion; Xiancheng rejoiced at receiving the commander's baton and banner. Though outwardly he obeyed the court's intent, inwardly he stood in mutual support with Zhu and Wang — this was in the first month of the second year of Changqing.

units.zh: 尋遣司門郎中韋文恪宣慰。
units.en: Before long the court sent Wei Wenke of the Gate Division, Bureau of State Affairs, as an envoy to offer consolation and reassurance.
units.literal: Soon the court dispatched Wei Wenke of the Department of State Affairs, Gate Division, as imperial envoy to offer consolation.

units.zh: 時李㝏爲亂，與憲誠書問交通。
units.en: Li Qi was then in rebellion and kept up a correspondence with Xiancheng.
units.literal: At the time Li Qi was in rebellion and exchanged letters with Xiancheng.

units.zh: 憲誠表請與㝏節鉞，仍於黎陽艤舟，示欲渡河。
units.en: Xiancheng memorialized asking for the same command baton as Qi, and moored boats at Liyang as if preparing to cross the river.
units.literal: Xiancheng memorialized requesting the same military commission as Qi, and moreover anchored boats at Liyang to show intent to cross the river.

units.zh: 及見文恪，舉止驕倨，其言甚悖。
units.en: When he received Wenke, his manner was haughty and his words openly defiant.
units.literal: When he met Wenke, his bearing was proud and arrogant, and his words were greatly rebellious.

units.zh: 旋聞絺爲帳下所殺，乃從改過，謂文恪曰：「憲誠蕃人，猶狗也，唯能識主。
units.en: When he soon heard that Qi had been killed by his own officers, he changed his tune and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian—no better than a dog—and knows only his master.
units.literal: Soon hearing that Qi had been killed by his subordinates, he then changed his ways and said to Wenke: "Xiancheng is a barbarian, like a dog — he can only recognize his master.

units.zh: 雖被棒打，終不忍離。」
units.en: Beat him as you will with a stick, yet he cannot bear to leave his master's side."
units.literal: Even if beaten with a stick, he could never bear to leave."

units.zh: 其狡譎如此。
units.en: Such was the depth of his cunning.
units.literal: Such was his cunning and deceit.

units.zh: 朝廷每爲優容，尋加左僕射。
units.en: The court repeatedly indulged him, and soon promoted him to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: The court repeatedly showed him forbearance, and soon added the post of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 敬宗即位，進秩司空。
units.en: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, Xiancheng was advanced to Grand Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, he was promoted to Grand Minister of Works.

units.zh: 太和二年，滄景節度使李全略卒，其子同捷竊據軍城，表邀符節，舉兵伐之。
units.en: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the garrison city and memorialized for the commander's seal and baton, whereupon the court mobilized an army against him.
units.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the military city by stealth, memorialized requesting the seal and baton of command, and the court raised troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 先是，憲誠與全略婚媾，及同捷叛，復潛以糧餉爲助。
units.en: Xiancheng had earlier been linked to Quanlue by marriage; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly supplied him with grain and fodder.
units.literal: Earlier Xiancheng had been allied by marriage with Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly aided him with provisions.

units.zh: 上屢發使申諭，尋又就加平章事。
units.en: The emperor sent envoys again and again to warn him, and soon added the title of Grand Councilor as well.
units.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to instruct and admonish him, and soon additionally appointed him Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 憲誠嘗遣驍將至闕下，恣爲張大，宰相韋處厚以語折剉之，憲誠不敢復與同捷爲應。
units.en: Xiancheng once sent bold generals to the capital who swaggered without restraint; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou put them down with sharp words, and Xiancheng no longer dared to act in concert with Tongjie.
units.literal: Xiancheng once sent fierce generals to the capital who acted with reckless arrogance; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuked them with words, and Xiancheng dared not again coordinate with Tongjie.

units.zh: 時憲誠示出師共討同捷。
units.en: For a time Xiancheng made a show of marching out to join the campaign against Tongjie.
units.literal: At the time Xiancheng made a show of setting out with troops to join in attacking Tongjie together.

units.zh: 及滄景平，加司徒。
units.en: When Cangjing was pacified, he was made Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When Cangjing was pacified, he was promoted to Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 憲誠心不自安，乃遣子孝章入覲，又飛章願以所管奉命。
units.en: Uneasy in his own mind, Xiancheng sent his son Xiaozhang to court and dispatched urgent memorials offering to place his command under the throne's orders.
units.literal: Xiancheng felt ill at ease in his heart; he then sent his son Xiaozhang to court for audience, and also sent urgent memorials offering to place his jurisdiction under court command.

units.zh: 上嘉之。
units.en: The emperor praised his loyalty.
units.literal: The emperor commended this.

units.zh: 乃加侍中，移鎮河中。
units.en: He was made Palace Attendant and transferred to Hezhong.
units.literal: He was then made Palace Attendant and transferred to govern Hezhong.

units.zh: 憲誠素懷向背，不能以忠誠感激其眾。
units.en: Xiancheng had long wavered between loyalty and defiance and could not win his troops over with steadfast devotion.
units.literal: Xiancheng had long harbored divided loyalties and could not move his followers with sincerity and devotion.

units.zh: 未及出城，太和三年六月二十六日夜，爲軍眾所害，冊贈太尉。
units.en: Before he could even leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month in the third year of Taihe, his own soldiers killed him; the court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Before he could leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of the third year of Taihe, he was killed by the troops; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 憲誠子 孝章孝章，幼聰悟好學。
units.en: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang was clever from childhood and devoted to study.
units.literal: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang — from youth he was clever and fond of learning.

units.zh: 元和中，李醞爲魏帥，取大將子弟列於軍籍。
units.en: During the Yuanhe reign, when Li Yun commanded Wei, he enrolled the sons of senior generals on the army rolls.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Li Yun was military governor of Wei; he enrolled the sons of senior generals on the army rolls.

units.zh: 孝章倡言願效文職，醞奇之，令攝府參軍。
units.en: Xiaozhang spoke up saying he wished to serve in the civil branch; Yun was impressed and appointed him acting headquarters adjutant.
units.literal: Xiaozhang openly declared that he wished to serve in a civil post; Yun was struck by this and had him act as staff adjutant of the headquarters.

units.zh: 及憲誠領節鉞，改士曹參軍、兼監察御史，賜緋。
units.en: When Xiancheng took the command baton, Xiaozhang was made Staff Officer of the Personnel Section and concurrent Investigating Censor, with scarlet robes bestowed on him.
units.literal: When Xiancheng received the military commission, Xiaozhang was changed to Staff Officer of the Personnel Section, concurrent Investigating Censor, and granted scarlet robes.

units.zh: 孝章以父在鎮多違朝旨，嘗雪涕極諫，備陳逆順之理。
units.en: Seeing that his father at his post often defied the court, Xiaozhang once wept as he remonstrated with all his strength, laying out in full the difference between loyalty and treason.
units.literal: Because his father at his post often defied the court's orders, Xiaozhang once wept as he remonstrated to the utmost, fully setting forth the principles of loyalty and rebellion.

units.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，乃授檢校太子左諭德、兼侍御史，充節度副使。
units.en: When the court heard of this it praised him and appointed him Acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Attending Censor, and deputy military governor.
units.literal: The court heard of this and commended him, then appointed him Acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Attending Censor, and deputy military governor.

units.zh: 累遷至散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，賜紫。
units.en: He rose in time to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted purple robes.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and granted purple robes.

units.zh: 領本道兵同平滄景，加工部尚書。
units.en: He led his circuit's troops in the pacification of Cangjing and was made Minister of Public Works.
units.literal: Leading troops of his circuit he joined in pacifying Cangjing, and was made Minister of the Ministry of Works.

units.zh: 尋請赴闕，文宗慰勞甚厚，憲誠亦因懇乞朝覲。
units.en: He soon asked leave to come to court; Emperor Wenzong received him with generous praise, and Xiancheng too pressed his petition to attend in person.
units.literal: Soon he requested to go to court; Emperor Wenzong comforted and rewarded him generously, and Xiancheng also earnestly begged to attend court.

units.zh: 上知憲誠之入覲，自孝章之謀，遂加禮部尚書，分相、衞、澶三州別爲一鎮，俾孝章領之。
units.en: The emperor understood that Xiancheng's wish to attend court came from Xiaozhang's counsel; he therefore made Xiaozhang Minister of Rites, carved out Xiang, Wei, and Chan as a separate command, and put Xiaozhang in charge of it.
units.literal: The emperor knew that Xiancheng's coming to court sprang from Xiaozhang's plan; he then added the post of Minister of Rites, separated the three prefectures of Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate command, and had Xiaozhang govern it.

units.zh: 孝章未到鎮，憲誠遇害。
units.en: Before Xiaozhang could reach his new command, Xiancheng was killed.
units.literal: Before Xiaozhang reached his post, Xiancheng met a violent death.

units.zh: 上以孝章有忠節，起復爲右金吾衞將軍。
units.en: The emperor, honoring Xiaozhang's loyal conduct, recalled him from mourning to be General of the Right Jinwu Guard.
units.literal: Because Xiaozhang had shown loyal integrity, the emperor recalled him from mourning to serve as General of the Right Jinwu Guard.

units.zh: 間歲，授鄜坊節度使。
units.en: A year later he was made military governor of Yan-Fang.
units.literal: Within a year he was appointed military governor of Yan and Fang.

units.zh: 居四年，遷於滑。
units.en: After four years he was transferred to Hua.
units.literal: After four years he was transferred to Hua.

units.zh: 一歲，入爲右領軍大將軍，改右金吾大將軍，俄授邠寧節度。
units.en: After a year he came to court as Grand General of the Right Leading Army, was reassigned as Grand General of the Right Jinwu Army, and soon received the Bian-Ning command.
units.literal: After one year he entered court as Grand General of the Right Leading Army, was changed to Grand General of the Right Jinwu Army, and soon received the Bian and Ning military governorship.

units.zh: 孝章歷三鎮，雖無異績，而謹身畏法，以保初終。
units.en: Xiaozhang held three commands; though he won no striking victories, he kept himself within the law and preserved his position from first to last.
units.literal: Xiaozhang governed three commands; though he had no outstanding achievements, he was scrupulous in conduct and feared the law, thereby preserving himself from beginning to end.

units.zh: 開成三年十月卒，贈右僕射。
units.en: He died in the tenth month of the third year of Kaicheng and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: He died in the tenth month of the third year of Kaicheng and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 何進滔，靈武人也。
units.en: He Jintao came from Lingwu.
units.literal: He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.

units.zh: 曾祖孝物，祖俊，並本州軍校。
units.en: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and his grandfather Jun had both been army officers in their home prefecture.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun were both army officers of the prefecture.

units.zh: 父默，夏州衙前兵馬使，檢校太子賓客，試太常卿。
units.en: His father Mo had served as horse-and-foot commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, with the ranks of Acting Crown Prince's Guest and Acting Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: His father Mo was Cavalry and Infantry Commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, and Acting Taichang Qing.

units.zh: 以進滔之貴，贈左散騎常侍。
units.en: When Jintao rose to high rank, Mo was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: Because of Jintao's eminence, Mo was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。
units.en: Jintao had settled in Wei as an outsider, pledged himself to the army, and served under the military governor Tian Hongzheng.
units.literal: Jintao lived as a guest in Wei, pledged himself to the army gate, and served the military governor Tian Hongzheng.

units.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔爲衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。
units.en: When Hongzheng marched on Yanzhou by imperial order and broke Li Shidao, Jintao was chief controller of horse and foot in the headquarters guard and was made concurrent Attending Censor for his service.
units.literal: Hongzheng received the edict to campaign against Yanzhou and defeated Li Shidao; at the time Jintao was Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry within the headquarters guard, and for his merit was appointed concurrent Attending Censor.

units.zh: 太和三年，軍眾害史憲誠，連聲而呼曰：「得衙內都知兵馬使何端公知留後，即三軍安矣。」
units.en: In the third year of Taihe the soldiers killed Shi Xiancheng and cried out together, "Let Lord He, the chief controller of the headquarters guard, take charge as acting governor, and the three armies will be settled."
units.literal: In the third year of Taihe the troops killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted in unison: "If the Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry within the headquarters guard, Lord He of Duan, becomes acting military governor, the three armies will be at peace."

units.zh: 推而立之。
units.en: They pressed him forward and set him up as their leader.
units.literal: They pushed him forward and installed him.

units.zh: 朝廷因授進滔左散騎常侍、魏博等州節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Weibo and the associated prefectures.
units.literal: The court accordingly appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Weibo and other prefectures.

units.zh: 爲魏帥十餘年，大得民情，累官至司徒、平章事卒。
units.en: He commanded Wei for more than ten years and won deep popular affection, rose through the ranks to Grand Tutor and Grand Councilor, and died in office.
units.literal: He was military governor of Wei for more than ten years, greatly winning the people's hearts, rose in office to Grand Tutor and Grand Councilor, and died.

units.zh: 進滔子 弘敬子弘敬襲其位。
units.en: Jintao's son Hongjing succeeded to his father's post.
units.literal: Jintao's son Hongjing — Hongjing succeeded to his position.

units.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。
units.en: The court had Li Zhifang of Hezhong and Liu Yue of Cangzhou each send envoys urging him to come to court and await further imperial orders.
units.literal: The court at the time had the commanders of Hezhong, Li Zhifang, and Cangzhou, Liu Yue, each send envoys urging him to return to court and await separate court orders.

units.zh: 弘敬不從，竟就加節制。
units.en: Hongjing refused, and in the end received the full command baton anyway.
units.literal: Hongjing did not comply and in the end received the full military commission.

units.zh: 及劉稹反，不時起兵。
units.en: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he failed to mobilize his troops promptly.
units.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he did not raise troops at the proper time.

units.zh: 鎮州王元逵下邢、洺二州，兵次上黨，弘敬方出師壓境。
units.en: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou had already taken Xing and Ming and halted his army at Shangdang before Hongjing at last marched out to menace the frontier.
units.literal: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou took the two prefectures of Xing and Ming; his troops halted at Shangdang, and only then did Hongjing march out to press the border.

units.zh: 大中後，宣宗務其姑息，繼加官爵，亦至使相。
units.en: After the Dazhong reign, Emperor Xuanzong treated him with deliberate indulgence, heaping rank upon rank until he too stood among the commissioners who held councilor titles.
units.literal: After the Dazhong era, Emperor Xuanzong pursued a policy of indulgence toward him, repeatedly adding offices and titles until he too reached the rank of commissioner and councilor.

units.zh: 咸通初，卒。
units.en: Early in the Xiantong reign he died.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he died.

units.zh: 子全皞嗣之。
units.en: His son Quanhao succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Quanhao succeeded him.

units.zh: 朝廷尋降符節，累官亦至同平章事。
units.en: The court soon granted him the commander's seal and baton, and in time he too rose to Concurrent Grand Councilor.
units.literal: The court soon bestowed the seal and baton; through successive promotions he too reached Concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 十一年，爲軍人所害。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Xiantong his own soldiers killed him.
units.literal: In the eleventh year he was killed by the soldiers.

units.zh: 子孫相繼，四十餘年。
units.en: Father and son held the post in succession for more than forty years.
units.literal: Father and son succeeded one another for more than forty years.

units.zh: 韓允忠，魏州人也。
units.en: Han Yunzhong came from Weizhou.
units.literal: Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 舊名君雄，懿宗改賜今名。
units.en: He had formerly been called Junxiong; Emperor Yizong granted him his present name.
units.literal: His former name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed and bestowed his present name.

units.zh: 父國昌，歷本州右職。
units.en: His father Guochang had held senior posts in the prefecture.
units.literal: His father Guochang held senior posts in the prefecture.

units.zh: 會昌中，從何弘敬破劉稹，以功爲貝州刺史、兼御史中丞。
units.en: During the Huichang reign he followed He Hongjing in the defeat of Liu Zhen and for his service was made prefect of Bei and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen and for his merit was made Prefect of Bei and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 以允忠故，累贈兵部尚書。
units.en: On Yunzhong's account, Guochang was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Minister of War.
units.literal: Because of Yunzhong, Guochang was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Minister of War.

units.zh: 允忠少仕軍門，繼升裨校。
units.en: Yunzhong entered military service young and rose through the ranks to staff officer.
units.literal: Yunzhong entered the army gate in youth and was promoted in succession to staff officer.

units.zh: 潞州之役，亦與其行。
units.en: He also took part in the campaign against Luzhou.
units.literal: In the Luzhou campaign he also marched with the army.

units.zh: 咸通十一年，何全皞爲軍眾所殺，推允忠爲帥。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Xiantong, when He Quanhao was killed by his soldiers, they set Yunzhong up as their leader.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Xiantong, He Quanhao was killed by the troops, and they pushed Yunzhong forward as commander.

units.zh: 時僖宗爲普王，即降詔遙領節度，授允忠左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞，充節度觀察留後。
units.en: Emperor Xizong was then still Prince of Pu; an edict at once named him to hold the command in absentia and appointed Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and acting military governor and observation commissioner.
units.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; an edict was immediately issued appointing him to hold the military governorship in absentia, and Yunzhong was made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Acting Military Governor and Observation Commissioner.

units.zh: 不數月，轉檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、充魏博節度觀察等使。
units.en: Within a few months he was made Acting Minister of Public Works, chief administrator of the superior prefecture of Weizhou, and military governor and observation commissioner of Weibo.
units.literal: Within a few months he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of the Superior Prefecture of Weizhou, and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Weibo.

units.zh: 累加至檢校司空、同平章事。
units.en: He rose in time to Acting Grand Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Acting Grand Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 乾符元年十一月卒，年六十一。
units.en: He died in the eleventh month of the first year of Qianfu, at the age of sixty-one.
units.literal: He died in the eleventh month of the first year of Qianfu, aged sixty-one.

units.zh: 累贈太尉。
units.en: He was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 允忠子 簡子簡，自允忠初授戎帥，便爲節度副使。
units.en: Yunzhong's son Jian had served as deputy military governor from the moment his father first took command.
units.literal: Yunzhong's son Jian — Jian, from the time Yunzhong first received the military command, served as deputy military governor.

units.zh: 乾符初，累官至檢校工部尚書。
units.en: By the opening of the Qianfu reign he had risen to Acting Minister of Public Works.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu he had risen in office to Acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 允忠卒，即起復爲節度觀察留後。
units.en: When Yunzhong died, Jian was recalled from mourning at once to serve as acting military governor and observation commissioner.
units.literal: When Yunzhong died, Jian was immediately recalled from mourning to serve as Acting Military Governor and Observation Commissioner.

units.zh: 逾月，加檢校右僕射。
units.en: After a month he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: After more than a month he was added Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 其後累加至侍中，封昌黎郡王。
units.en: He was later promoted to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli.
units.literal: Thereafter he was promoted in succession to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli commandery.

units.zh: 賊巢之亂，諸葛爽受其偽命河陽節度使。
units.en: During Huang Chao's rebellion, Zhuge Shuang accepted a bogus appointment from him as military governor of Heyang.
units.literal: During the rebellion of the bandit Huang Chao, Zhuge Shuang received from him a false appointment as military governor of Heyang.

units.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，寇盜蜂起，簡據有六州，甲兵強盛，竊懷僭亂之志，且欲啟其封疆，乃舉兵攻河陽，爽棄城而走。
units.en: The emperor was then in Shu while rebels swarmed the land. Jian held six prefectures and a powerful army; nursing secret ambitions of rebellion and eager to enlarge his domain, he marched on Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.
units.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; bandits and robbers swarmed forth. Jian held six prefectures, his armor and troops were strong, and he secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation and wished to expand his territory; he therefore raised troops to attack Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 簡遂留兵保守，因北掠邢、洺而歸，遂移軍攻鄆。
units.en: Jian left troops to hold Heyang, raided north through Xing and Ming, then turned his army against Yan.
units.literal: Jian then left troops to hold and defend the place, raided north through Xing and Ming and returned, then shifted his army to attack Yan.

units.zh: 鄆帥曹全晸出戰，爲簡所敗，死之。
units.en: Cao Quanzhen, governor of Yan, marched out to meet him, was defeated, and was killed.
units.literal: Cao Quanzhen, military governor of Yan, went out to battle and was defeated by Jian and killed.

units.zh: 鄆將崔君裕收合殘眾，保鄆州。
units.en: The Yan officer Cui Junyu rallied the survivors and held Yanzhou.
units.literal: The Yan general Cui Junyu gathered the scattered remnants and held Yan prefecture.

units.zh: 簡進攻其城，半年不下，河陽復爲諸葛爽所襲。
units.en: Jian besieged the city for half a year without success, while Heyang was seized again by Zhuge Shuang.
units.literal: Jian pressed the attack on the city for half a year without taking it; Heyang was again seized by Zhuge Shuang.

units.zh: 簡因欲先討君裕，次及河陽，乃舉兵至鄆，君裕請降。
units.en: Jian resolved to deal with Junyu first and Heyang afterward; he marched on Yan, and Junyu offered to surrender.
units.literal: Jian therefore wished first to subdue Junyu and afterward deal with Heyang; he raised troops and came to Yan, and Junyu requested surrender.

units.zh: 尋移軍復攻河陽，行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊，敗之。
units.en: He soon marched on Heyang again, but near Xinxiang, Shuang's troops met him head-on and routed him.
units.literal: Soon he shifted his army to attack Heyang again; when he reached Xinxing he was struck in counterattack by Shuang's army and defeated.

units.zh: 簡單騎奔回，憂憤。
units.en: Jian fled back alone on horseback, sick with grief and rage.
units.literal: Jian fled back alone on horseback, stricken with grief and anger.

units.zh: 疽發背而卒，時中和元年十一月也。
units.en: A carbuncle broke out between his shoulders and he died, in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.
units.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died — this was in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.

units.zh: 樂彥禎，魏州人也。
units.en: Le Yanzhen came from Weizhou.
units.literal: Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 父少寂，歷澶、博、貝三州刺史，贈工部尚書。
units.en: His father Shaoji had governed Chan, Bo, and Bei in turn and was posthumously made Minister of Public Works.
units.literal: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei, and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 彥禎少爲本州軍校。
units.en: Yanzhen began his career as an army officer in his home prefecture.
units.literal: In youth Yanzhen was an army officer of the prefecture.

units.zh: 韓簡之領節旄也，以彥禎爲馬歩軍都虞候，轉博州刺史。
units.en: When Han Jian took command, he made Yanzhen chief commandant of the horse and foot armies and later made him prefect of Bo.
units.literal: When Han Jian held the command baton, he made Yanzhen Chief Commandant of Horse and Foot Armies and then transferred him to be Prefect of Bo.

units.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。
units.en: He captured Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang from the field.
units.literal: He took Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang to flight.

units.zh: 有功，遷澶州刺史。
units.en: For this service he was transferred to Chan.
units.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Prefect of Chan.

units.zh: 簡再討河陽之敗也。
units.en: This was during Han Jian's second, failed campaign against Heyang.
units.literal: This was when Jian again campaigned against Heyang and was defeated.

units.zh: 彥禎以一軍先歸，魏人遂共立之。
units.en: Yanzhen brought one division home ahead of the rest, and the men of Wei promptly set him up as their leader.
units.literal: Yanzhen returned first with one army, and the people of Wei thereupon jointly installed him.

units.zh: 朝廷尋授檢校工部尚書，知魏博留後。
units.en: The court soon made him Acting Minister of Public Works and acting governor of Weibo.
units.literal: The court soon appointed him Acting Minister of Works and Acting Military Governor of Weibo.

units.zh: 俄加戸部尚書，充節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: He was soon made Minister of Revenue and full military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner.
units.literal: Soon he was added Minister of Revenue and made Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner.

units.zh: 中和四年，累加至尚書左僕射、同平章事。
units.en: By the fourth year of Zhonghe he had risen to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhonghe he was promoted in succession to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 僖宗自蜀回，加開府儀同三司，冊拜司徒。
units.en: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen received the honorary rank of Grand General of the Palace with the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen was added Grand General of the Palace with the Honorary Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 彥禎志滿驕大，動多不法。
units.en: Once his ambitions were satisfied, Yanzhen grew proud and overbearing, and his conduct was often lawless.
units.literal: Yanzhen's ambitions were fulfilled and he became proud and overbearing, and his actions were often unlawful.

units.zh: 一旦征六州之眾，板築羅城，約河門舊堤，周八十里，月餘而畢，人用怨咨。
units.en: On one occasion he drafted the levies of all six prefectures to build an outer wall along the old Hemen embankment, eighty li around; though the work took only a month, the people groaned under it.
units.literal: One day he conscripted the forces of the six prefectures to build a walled outer city along the old embankment at Hemen, eighty li in circuit; it was completed in more than a month, and the people murmured in resentment.

units.zh: 彥禎子 從訓又其子從訓天資悖逆。
units.en: Yanzhen's son Congxun was violent and defiant by nature.
units.literal: Yanzhen's son Congxun — moreover his son Congxun was by nature rebellious and perverse.

units.zh: 王鐸自滑移鎮滄州，過魏郊，從訓見其女妓，利之，先伏兵於漳南高雞泊，俟鐸之至，圍而害之，掠其所有。
units.en: When Wang Duo was transferred from Hua to Cangzhou and passed through Wei's borderlands, Congxun saw his female entertainers and coveted them. He ambushed troops at Gaojipo south of Zhang, surrounded Duo when he arrived, killed him, and looted all he possessed.
units.literal: Wang Duo was transferred from Hua to govern Cangzhou and passed through the outskirts of Wei; Congxun saw his female entertainers and coveted them. He first hid troops at Gaojipo south of Zhang, waited until Duo arrived, surrounded him, and killed him, plundering everything he had.

units.zh: 時朝廷微弱，不能詰。
units.en: The court was then too weak to call him to account.
units.literal: At the time the court was weak and could not investigate.

units.zh: 魏人素知鐸名望，議者惜之，而罪從訓。
units.en: The men of Wei had long respected Duo's standing; public opinion mourned him and condemned Congxun.
units.literal: The people of Wei had long known Duo's reputation; commentators regretted his death and blamed Congxun.

units.zh: 從訓又召亡命之徒五百餘輩，出入臥內，號爲「子將」，委以腹心。
units.en: Congxun also gathered more than five hundred outlaws who moved freely in and out of his private quarters, styled them "son-commanders," and treated them as his inner circle.
units.literal: Congxun also summoned more than five hundred outlaws who came and went within his sleeping quarters, called them "son-commanders," and entrusted them with his innermost affairs.

units.zh: 軍人籍籍，各有異議。
units.en: Rumors spread through the ranks, and opinion was divided.
units.literal: Among the soldiers there was much whispering, and each held a different view.

units.zh: 從訓聞而忌之，易服遁出，止於近縣。
units.en: Hearing of this, Congxun grew wary, disguised himself, slipped away, and lodged in a nearby county.
units.literal: Congxun heard of this and grew suspicious; he changed clothes and slipped out, stopping in a nearby county.

units.zh: 彥禎因命爲六州都指揮使。
units.en: Yanzhen then appointed him commander-in-chief over the six prefectures.
units.literal: Yanzhen therefore appointed him Commander-in-Chief of the Six Prefectures.

units.zh: 未幾，又兼相州刺史。
units.en: Soon afterward he was made concurrent prefect of Xiang as well.
units.literal: Before long he was also made concurrently Prefect of Xiang.

units.zh: 到任之後，般輦軍器，取索錢帛，使人來往，交午塗路，軍府疑貳。
units.en: Once in office he hauled off military stores and extorted cash and silk until couriers thronged the roads and the headquarters grew uneasy.
units.literal: After he took up his post he transported military equipment and extorted money and silk; messengers came and went until the roads were crowded, and the headquarters grew doubtful and uneasy.

units.zh: 彥禎危憤而卒，眾推都將趙文㺹知留後事。
units.en: Yanzhen died, broken with anger and fear; the troops set up the chief commander Zhao Wenqing to manage affairs as acting governor.
units.literal: Yanzhen died in distress and indignation; the masses pushed forward the chief commander Zhao Wenqing to handle affairs as acting governor.

units.zh: 從訓自相州領兵三萬餘人至城下，文㺹按兵不出。
units.en: Congxun marched from Xiang with more than thirty thousand men and halted beneath the walls; Wenqing kept his army inside and refused battle.
units.literal: Congxun led more than thirty thousand men from Xiang to the city walls; Wenqing held his troops and would not come out.

units.zh: 眾懷疑懼，復害文㺹，推羅弘信爲帥。
units.en: The army grew fearful and restless; they killed Wenqing in turn and set up Luo Hongxin as commander.
units.literal: The masses were suspicious and afraid; they again killed Wenqing and pushed Luo Hongxin forward as commander.

units.zh: 弘信以兵出戰，敗之。
units.en: Hongxin took the field and defeated him.
units.literal: Hongxin went out to battle with troops and defeated him.

units.zh: 從訓招集餘眾，次於洹水。
units.en: Congxun rallied his survivors and encamped on the Huan River.
units.literal: Congxun gathered the scattered remnants and encamped at the Huan River.

units.zh: 弘信遣將程公佐領兵討擊，大敗之，梟從訓首於軍門，時文德元年春也。
units.en: Hongxin sent Cheng Gongzuo in pursuit, routed him utterly, and displayed Congxun's head before the army gate in the spring of the first year of Wende.
units.literal: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack; he inflicted a great defeat and displayed Congxun's head at the army gate — this was in the spring of the first year of Wende.

units.zh: 羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄕人。
units.en: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, came from Guixiang in Weizhou.
units.literal: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, was a man of Guixiang in Weizhou.

units.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆爲本州軍校。
units.en: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been army officers in the prefecture.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been army officers of the prefecture.

units.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。
units.en: Hongxin entered military service young and served in turn under Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.
units.literal: In youth Hongxin followed military service and successively served the military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.

units.zh: 光啟末，彥禎子從訓忌牙軍，出居於外，軍眾廢彥禎，推趙文㺹權主軍州事。
units.en: Late in the Guangqi reign, Congxun, fearing the yajiun, withdrew to an outside post; the soldiers deposed Yanzhen and set Zhao Wenqing to govern the circuit provisionally.
units.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun, fearing the yajiun, went out to live elsewhere; the troops deposed Yanzhen and pushed Zhao Wenqing to provisionally govern the army and prefecture.

units.zh: 眾復以爲不便，因推弘信爲帥。
units.en: The troops soon found this arrangement unsatisfactory and set up Hongxin instead.
units.literal: The masses again found this unsuitable and therefore pushed Hongxin forward as commander.

units.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當爲土地主。
units.en: Earlier a neighbor had told him in private, "One night I met a white-bearded old man who said you would become lord of this land.
units.literal: Earlier a neighbor had secretly told Hongxin: "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who told me that you would become master of the land.

units.zh: 如是者再三。」
units.en: He said it again and again."
units.literal: This happened again and again."

units.zh: 弘信竊異之。
units.en: Hongxin kept the story to himself and wondered at it.
units.literal: Hongxin secretly marveled at this.

units.zh: 及廢文㺹，軍人聚呼曰：「孰願爲節度使者？」
units.en: When Wenqing was removed, the soldiers cried out together, "Who will be military governor?"
units.literal: When Wenqing was deposed, the soldiers gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military governor?"

units.zh: 弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。」
units.en: Hongxin answered at once, "The white-bearded old man appointed me long ago."
units.literal: Hongxin immediately answered: "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."

units.zh: 眾乃環而視之，曰：「可也。」
units.en: The men ringed him round and said, "He will do."
units.literal: The masses then surrounded and looked at him, saying: "He will do."

units.zh: 由是立之。
units.en: So they set him up as their leader.
units.literal: Thereupon they installed him.

units.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。
units.en: When Emperor Xizong learned of it, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende he was made Minister of Public Works and authorized as acting military governor.
units.literal: When Emperor Xizong heard of this, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende an edict added the post of Minister of Works and authorized him to act as Acting Military Governor.

units.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: In the seventh month he was further made Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Weibo.
units.literal: In the seventh month he was again added Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Weibo.

units.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。
units.en: During the Longji reign he was made Acting Grand Minister of Works, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Duke of Yuzhang.
units.literal: In the Longji era he was added Acting Grand Minister of Works, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.

units.zh: 乾寧中，朱全忠急攻兗鄆，朱瑄求援於太原。
units.en: During Qianning, Zhu Quanzhong pressed Yan and Yun hard, and Zhu Xuan appealed to Taiyuan for help.
units.literal: In the Qianning era Zhu Quanzhong pressed the attack on Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.

units.zh: 太原發軍，假道於魏，令大將李存信屯莘縣。
units.en: Taiyuan marched an army through Wei and stationed the great general Li Cunxin at Shen county.
units.literal: Taiyuan sent out an army and asked passage through Wei; the great general Li Cunxin was stationed at Shen county.

units.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。
units.en: Cunxin kept poor discipline and plundered Wei's fodder and pasture, to Hongxin's anger.
units.literal: Cunxin governed his troops without discipline and encroached on Wei's fodder and pasture; Hongxin was displeased.

units.zh: 全忠復遣人謂之曰：「太原志吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。」
units.en: Quanzhong sent word again: "Taiyuan means to swallow the Hebei region; when it turns homeward, your circuit will be in peril."
units.literal: Quanzhong again sent someone to tell him: "Taiyuan intends to swallow the Hebei region; on the day it turns its spears back, your circuit will be in peril."

units.zh: 弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。
units.en: Hongxin therefore courted Bian, marched out thirty thousand men against Cunxin, and defeated him.
units.literal: Hongxin therefore made a show of friendship with Bian and marched out thirty thousand men to attack Cunxin and defeated him.

units.zh: 太原怒，舉兵攻魏，營於觀音門外。
units.en: Taiyuan was furious, marched on Wei, and encamped outside the Guanyin Gate.
units.literal: Taiyuan was enraged and raised troops to attack Wei, encamping outside the Guanyin Gate.

units.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。
units.en: Ge Congzhou of Bian came to his relief and encamped on the Huan River.
units.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to his aid and encamped at the Huan River.

units.zh: 李克用子落落時爲鐵林軍使，爲從周所擒，乃退歸。
units.en: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and Taiyuan withdrew.
units.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was then Iron Forest Army commander; he was captured by Congzhou and Taiyuan then withdrew.

units.zh: 自是太原之師，每歲侵擾相、魏，魏人患之。
units.en: Thereafter Taiyuan raided Xiang and Wei year after year, to the great distress of the Wei people.
units.literal: From this time the armies of Taiyuan each year harassed Xiang and Wei, and the people of Wei suffered from them.

units.zh: 朱全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。
units.en: Quanzhong was then busy with Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might waver; every season he sent gifts, and Hongxin always replied with humble words and lavish return gifts.
units.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yun and feared that Hongxin might turn aside; every year at the seasons he sent gifts, and Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous return gifts.

units.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。」
units.en: Quanzhong would face north and bow to receive Wei's gifts, saying, "Sixth Brother is more than twice my age; we are brothers in arms — how could I treat him as an ordinary neighbor?"
units.literal: Quanzhong, facing Wei's envoy, bowed toward the north to receive the gifts and said: "Sixth Brother is more than twice my age; we are a state of brothers — how can I treat him as an ordinary neighbor?"

units.zh: 弘信以爲厚己，亦推心焉。
units.en: Hongxin took this as genuine regard and gave Quanzhong his full trust in return.
units.literal: Hongxin thought he was treating him generously and also gave him his full trust.

units.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。
units.en: Hongxin rose in time to Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.
units.literal: Hongxin rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.

units.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。
units.en: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua at sixty-three; the court posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, Prince of Beiping, with the posthumous title Zhuangsu.
units.literal: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua, aged sixty-three; posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.

units.zh: 子威。
units.en: His son was Wei.
units.literal: His son was Wei.

units.zh: 弘信子 威威，字端己。
units.en: Hongxin's son Wei, styled Duanji.
units.literal: Hongxin's son Wei — Wei, styled Duanji.

units.zh: 文德初，授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使。
units.en: At the opening of Wende he was made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy military governor of the Tianxiong Army.
units.literal: At the beginning of Wende he was appointed Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy military governor of the Tianxiong Army.

units.zh: 自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵。
units.en: From Longji through Qianning he accumulated rank upon rank for ten years.
units.literal: From Longji through Qianning, within ten years he was repeatedly promoted in office and rank.

units.zh: 弘信卒，襲父位爲留後，朝廷從而命之。
units.en: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded as acting governor, and the court confirmed the appointment.
units.literal: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded to his father's post as acting governor, and the court accordingly appointed him.

units.zh: 天復末，累加至檢校太傅、兼侍中、長沙王。
units.en: By the end of Tianfu he had risen to Acting Grand Tutor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.
units.literal: At the end of Tianfu he was promoted in succession to Acting Grand Tutor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.

units.zh: 天祐初，授檢校太尉、守侍中，進封鄴王，賜號「忠勤宣力致理功臣」。
units.en: Early in Tianyou he was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Defender Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence in Ordering the Realm."
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was appointed Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence in Ordering the Realm."

units.zh: 魏之牙中軍者，自至德中，田承嗣盜據相、魏、澶、博、衞、貝等六州，召募軍中子弟置之部下，遂以爲號。
units.en: Wei's yajiun, the elite of the central army, dated from the Zhide era, when Tian Chengsi seized Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei and enrolled soldiers' sons in his personal following under that name.
units.literal: The yajiun of Wei's central army — from the Zhide era, when Tian Chengsi seized the six prefectures of Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei, he recruited sons of army families and placed them under his command, and they took this as their designation.

units.zh: 皆豐給厚賜，不勝驕寵。
units.en: They were lavishly paid and richly favored until pride knew no bounds.
units.literal: All were richly supplied and generously rewarded, beyond what pride and favor could bear.

units.zh: 年代浸遠，父子相襲，親黨膠固。
units.en: Over the generations father succeeded son and kin cliques grew entrenched.
units.literal: As the years lengthened, father and son succeeded one another and kin cliques grew rigid.

units.zh: 其凶戾者，強買豪奪，逾法犯令，長吏不能禁。
units.en: The worst among them extorted and seized by force, broke the law with impunity, and their superiors could not restrain them.
units.literal: The violent among them forcibly bought and seized by force, violated laws and orders, and the chief officials could not restrain them.

units.zh: 變易主帥，有同兒戲，如史憲誠、何進滔、韓君雄、樂彥禎，皆爲其所立。
units.en: They changed commanders as casually as children at play; Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen had all been set up by them.
units.literal: They changed commanders as easily as child's play; Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all installed by them.

units.zh: 優獎小不如意，則舉族被害。
units.en: If rewards fell the least bit short, whole clans were wiped out.
units.literal: If rewards and favors fell the least bit short, whole clans were destroyed.

units.zh: 威懲其往弊，雖以貨賂姑息，而心銜之。
units.en: Wei meant to break their old abuses; though he bought them off with gifts, he nursed hatred in his heart.
units.literal: Wei punished their past abuses; though he placated them with bribes, in his heart he resented them.

units.zh: 威嗣世之明年，正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。
units.en: In the first month of the second year of Wei's rule, Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched a hundred thousand men to stir trouble in Hebei, seized Bei, and drove straight at Wei.
units.literal: In the second year after Wei succeeded, in the first month, Liu Rengong of Youzhou gathered a hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in the Hebei region, advanced and took Bei prefecture, and drove straight to attack Wei.

units.zh: 威求援於汴。
units.en: Wei appealed to Bian for help.
units.literal: Wei sought aid from Bian.

units.zh: 朱全忠遣將李思安屯於洹水。
units.en: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to encamp on the Huan River.
units.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent the general Li Si'an to encamp at the Huan River.

units.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。
units.en: Ge Congzhou marched in from Xing and Ming.
units.literal: Ge Congzhou led troops from Xing and Ming into Wei.

units.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。
units.en: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian forces at Neihuang.
units.literal: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.

units.zh: 思安逆戰，大敗之，乘勝追躡。
units.en: Si'an met them in battle, routed them, and pursued in victory.
units.literal: Si'an met them in battle and inflicted a great defeat, then pursued in victory.

units.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。
units.en: Congzhou came out to strike in concert, crushed the Yan army, and took thirty thousand heads.
units.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a converging strike and annihilated the Yan army, beheading thirty thousand.

units.zh: 三年，威引汴軍攻滄州以報之。
units.en: In the third year Wei led Bian's army against Cangzhou in reprisal.
units.literal: In the third year Wei led Bian troops to attack Cangzhou in retaliation.

units.zh: 自是，威感全忠援助之恩，合從景附。
units.en: From then on Wei, grateful for Quanzhong's aid, clung to him in alliance.
units.literal: From this time Wei was moved by gratitude for Quanzhong's aid and drew close to him in alliance.

units.zh: 天祐二年七月十三日夜，牙軍裨校李公佺作亂，威僅以身免。
units.en: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month in the second year of Tianyou, the yajiun officer Li Gongquan rebelled, and Wei barely escaped with his life.
units.literal: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of the second year of Tianyou, the yajiun staff officer Li Gongquan rebelled; Wei barely escaped with his life.

units.zh: 公佺出奔滄州。
units.en: Gongquan fled to Cangzhou.
units.literal: Gongquan fled to Cangzhou.

units.zh: 自是愈懼，遣使求援於全忠，密謀破之。
units.en: Thereafter Wei grew ever more fearful, sent to Quanzhong for help, and secretly plotted their destruction.
units.literal: From this Wei grew ever more afraid; he sent envoys to seek aid from Quanzhong and secretly plotted to destroy them.

units.zh: 全忠遣李思安會魏博軍，再攻滄州。
units.en: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join the Weibo army in a renewed attack on Cangzhou.
units.literal: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join the Weibo army in again attacking Cangzhou.

units.zh: 全忠女妻威子廷規，先是卒。
units.en: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui and had died earlier.
units.literal: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had died earlier.

units.zh: 全忠遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，密於輿中實兵甲入魏，言助女葬事。
units.en: Quanzhong sent Ma Cixun of the long-service guard to choose a thousand men and smuggle arms into Wei in funeral litters, under the pretext of helping bury his daughter.
units.literal: Quanzhong sent the chief of the long-service guard Ma Cixun to select a thousand troops; arms and armor were secretly loaded in the palanquins that entered Wei, on the pretext of assisting with the daughter's funeral.

units.zh: 三年正月五日，嗣勳至，全忠親率大軍濟河，言視行營於滄景。
units.en: On the fifth day of the first month in the third year Cixun arrived; Quanzhong himself led a great army across the river, saying he meant to inspect the Cangjing front.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Cixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, saying he was going to inspect the camp at Cangjing.

units.zh: 威欲因而出迎，至期，即假全忠帳下銳卒入而夾攻之。
units.en: Wei planned to go out to meet him and, when the day came, borrow Quanzhong's crack troops to enter the city and strike the yajiun from within and without.
units.literal: Wei wished to go out to meet him; when the day came he would borrow sharp troops from Quanzhong's camp to enter and strike them from both sides.

units.zh: 牙軍頗疑，堅請不出。
units.en: The yajiun grew suspicious and insisted he not leave the city.
units.literal: The yajiun were quite suspicious and firmly begged him not to go out.

units.zh: 威恐洩其事，慰納之。
units.en: Fearing his plot would leak, Wei soothed and reassured them.
units.literal: Wei feared the plot would leak and comforted and appeased them.

units.zh: 是月十四日夜，率廝養百十輩，與嗣勳合攻之。
units.en: On the night of the fourteenth he led a hundred-odd personal retainers to join Cixun in the assault.
units.literal: On the night of the fourteenth day of that month he led a hundred or so personal attendants to join Cixun in a combined attack.

units.zh: 時宿於牙城者千人，遲明殺之殆盡；
units.en: A thousand yajiun were then quartered in the headquarters city; by dawn nearly all had been slaughtered;
units.literal: At the time a thousand men were quartered in the yamen city; by dawn they had been killed almost to the last man;

units.zh: 凡八千家，皆破其族。
units.en: eight thousand households in all had their clans destroyed.
units.literal: in all eight thousand households had their clans destroyed.

units.zh: 魏軍攻滄州者，在歷亭聞有變，其將史仁遇擁之，保於高唐。
units.en: The Wei troops besieging Cangzhou at Liting heard of the upheaval; their commander Shi Renyu held them together and defended Gaotang.
units.literal: Those of the Wei army attacking Cangzhou, at Liting, heard of the disturbance; their commander Shi Renyu held them together and defended Gaotang.

units.zh: 六州之內，皆爲讎敵，累月平之。
units.en: Throughout the six prefectures every survivor became an enemy; months passed before order was restored.
units.literal: Within the six prefectures all became enemies; it took months to pacify them.

units.zh: 威仕梁數年後卒，年三十四，位至守太師、兼中書令，贈尚書令，謚曰貞壯。
units.en: After several years in Liang service Wei died at thirty-four, having reached Defender Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat; the court posthumously made him Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Zhenzhuang.
units.literal: After serving Liang for several years Wei died, aged thirty-four; in office he reached Defender Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat; posthumously he was made Director of the Secretariat and given the posthumous title Zhenzhuang.

units.zh: 威性明敏，達於吏道。
units.en: Wei was quick-witted and thoroughly versed in administrative practice.
units.literal: Wei was by nature keen and perceptive and skilled in the ways of administration.

units.zh: 伏膺儒術，招納文人，聚書至萬卷。
units.en: He honored Confucian learning, gathered scholars, and amassed a library of ten thousand scrolls.
units.literal: He revered Confucian learning, recruited literary men, and gathered books to ten thousand volumes.

units.zh: 每花朝月夕，與賓佐賦詠，甚有情致。
units.en: On spring evenings and moonlit nights he would compose poetry with his guests and staff, always with real elegance and charm.
units.literal: On every flower-bright moonlit evening he joined his guests and aides in composing and reciting poetry, with much grace and feeling.

units.zh: 錢塘人羅隱者，有當世詩名，自號「江東生」。
units.en: Luo Yin of Qiantang was a poet of his day with a contemporary reputation; he styled himself "Jiangdong Sheng."
units.literal: Luo Yin of Qiantang enjoyed renown for poetry in his age and styled himself "Jiangdong Sheng."

units.zh: 威遣使賂遺，敘其宗姓，推爲叔父。
units.en: Wei sent envoys with gifts, laid out their shared clan ties, and honored him as an uncle.
units.literal: Wei sent envoys with gifts, recounted their shared clan surname, and treated him as an uncle.

units.zh: 隱亦集其詩寄之。
units.en: Yin in turn gathered his own poems and sent them to Wei.
units.literal: Yin also collected his poems and sent them to him.

units.zh: 威酷嗜其作，目己所爲曰《偷江東集》，凡五卷，今鄴中人士諷詠之。
units.en: Wei adored his poetry, titled his own compositions Collected Poems Stolen from Jiangdong in five volumes, and the people of Ye still recite them.
units.literal: Wei was passionately fond of his works, called his own compositions "Collected Poems Stolen from Jiangdong," five volumes in all; the people of Ye now recite and chant them.

units.zh: 史臣曰：魏、鎮、燕三鎮，不能制之也久矣。
units.en: The historiographer writes: The three commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan have long been beyond the court's control.
units.literal: The historiographer says: The three commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan — the court has long been unable to control them.

units.zh: 兵強地廣，合從連衡。
units.en: Their armies are strong and their territories vast; they league together in shifting alliances.
units.literal: Their troops are strong and their lands broad; they form alliances and vertical-horizontal coalitions.

units.zh: 爵命雖假於朝廷，群臣自謀於元帥。
units.en: Though rank and commission come from the throne, the ministers plot their own affairs under the warlords.
units.literal: Though titles and commands are borrowed from the court, the ministers plot among themselves under the warlords.

units.zh: 如史憲誠等五家，其初皆因此而得之，其後亦因此而失之。
units.en: The five houses, beginning with Shi Xiancheng, first rose by this means and later fell by it as well.
units.literal: Such were the five houses including Shi Xiancheng — at first they all gained power thereby, and later they all lost it thereby.

units.zh: 蓋不知取之以權，守之以仁，則遠矣。
units.en: They did not understand taking power through expedience and holding it through benevolence — how far they were from that wisdom.
units.literal: For they did not know how to seize power by expedient means and preserve it by benevolence — how far they were from this!

units.zh: 若善繼者，史氏、羅氏之二子有焉，其餘不足觀也。
units.en: Where succession went well, the sons of the Shi and Luo families may serve as examples; the rest are scarcely worth notice.
units.literal: Among those who succeeded well, the two sons of the Shi and Luo families qualify; the rest are not worth examining.

units.zh: 贊贊曰：逆取順守，古亦有之。
units.en: In praise it is said: To seize by force and rule by righteousness — even antiquity knew such cases.
units.literal: Praise says: To seize by rebellion and preserve by compliance — antiquity too has known this.

units.zh: 如其逆守，滅亡必隨。
units.en: But to hold power through rebellion is to invite ruin without fail.
units.literal: If one preserves by rebellion, destruction and extinction must follow.

units.zh: 史、何、韓、樂，世數盛衰。
units.en: The houses of Shi, He, Han, and Le rose and fell through the generations.
units.literal: Shi, He, Han, and Le — generations waxed and waned.

units.zh: 足以爲鑒，念茲在茲。
units.en: Let this be warning enough — and let it be kept ever in mind.
units.literal: This is sufficient to serve as a mirror; let this be borne in mind.
